title: Enterprise Onboarding: Integration, Escalation, Health Checks & QBR Playbook (v3)
author: Jordan Lee
body:
# Enterprise Onboarding: Integration, Escalation, Health Checks & QBR Playbook

Summary:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended processes and templates for enterprise customer onboarding across integration activities, escalation handling, known issues/workarounds, routine health checks, and Quarterly Business Review (QBR) preparation. Intended audience: Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and SREs.

Scope:
- Applies to enterprise customers onboarding to Redwood Hosted API, Dedicated, or Private deployments.
- Covers integration checkpoints, escalation routing and timelines, known issues and mitigations, weekly/monthly health checks, and QBR cadence and artifacts.

Owners and contacts:
- Playbook owner: Jordan Lee (Customer Success) - jordan.lee@redwood.ai
- Integration lead: Priya Desai (Solutions Engineering) - priya.desai@redwood.ai
- Escalation owner: Carlos Ruiz (Support Engineering) - carlos.ruiz@redwood.ai
- Operational escalation: On-call SRE via PagerDuty policy REDWOOD-ENTERPRISE-POLICY
- Slack channels: #support-enterprise, #onboarding-integrations, #sre-oncall

1) Pre-onboarding checklist (SE -> CSM handoff)
- Confirm contract & deployment mode (hosted / dedicated / private).
- Confirm primary technical and escalation contacts.
- Confirm data residency, retention, and KMS/HSM requirements.
- Provide API keys and least-privilege IAM roles for integration.
- Share usage profile: expected RPS, prompt length, peak windows, batch sizes.
- Schedule kickoff call (2 hours) with architecture, security, routing, and Q&A.

2) Integration Guide (technical checkpoints)
- Core services to validate: redwood-api (auth, rate limits), redwood-console (team access, billing), metrics & logging.
- Integration steps: 1) Validate API key and test generation request. 2) Confirm schema compatibility and function-calling. 3) Validate streaming and client chunk handling. 4) Verify prefix/KV cache behavior. 5) Run baseline load test and capture p50/p95/p99 and error rate. 6) Finalize routing for multi-region/dedicated fallbacks.

- Sample verification cURL: curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"Hello world","max_tokens":50}'

- Benchmarking template (sample targets): Test: Single-user interactive -> Target p95 < 400ms; Bulk embedding batch (128) -> < 2s per batch; Peak throughput -> matches committed qps.

3) Onboarding timeline (sample 6-week plan)
- Week 0: Contract & kickoff. Week 1: Initial integration & security review. Week 2: Load testing and tuning. Week 3: Failover and canary tests. Week 4: Security/pen test and compliance sign-off. Week 5: Pre-prod pilot. Week 6: Production cutover and 2-week stabilization.

4) Escalation playbook (support + SRE)
- Severity definitions: Sev1 Critical (total outage/data corruption); Sev2 High (major regression or >50% error rate); Sev3 Medium (partial impairment); Sev4 Low (informational).
- Timelines: Sev1 initial response <=15m, updates every 30m; Sev2 <=1h, updates every 2h; Sev3 <=4 business hours; Sev4 <=48h.
- Sev1 procedure: mark ticket Sev1 in Zendesk, notify #support-enterprise and PagerDuty, create incident doc, notify customer by phone/Slack, SRE runs diagnostics, execute emergency deploy if needed, postmortem within 3 business days.
- Escalation matrix: CS Jordan Lee -> Maya Patel; Support L2 Carlos Ruiz -> Daniel Murphy; SRE on-call via PagerDuty -> eng-sre lead.

5) Runbook: immediate diagnostics
- Collect account id, API key id, recent request ids, timestamps. Check redwood-console per-account metrics. Verify dependencies (DB, model-serving nodes, network). Runbooks: check-kv-cache-status, verify-model-pods-and-kv-cache, check-gpu-memory-pressure.
- Common commands: kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=model-serving -o wide; curl -s https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health | jq .; pd-trigger --policy REDWOOD-ENTERPRISE-POLICY --notify.

6) Known issues and workarounds (living table)
- Maintain in ticket and account record. Use labels: investigation, workaround_provided, fix_planned, fixed.
- Sample entries: KI-2025-21: Streaming chunk order mismatch on slow clients -> workaround: advise client reassembly by token index or disable streaming for critical flows; Status: workaround_provided; ETA 2026-04-15. KI-2026-08: Elevated p99 for long-context (8k+) on quantized models -> workaround: route to non-quantized variant or increase dedicated capacity; Status: fix_planned; ETA 2026-05-10.

7) Weekly / Monthly health checks
- Weekly (owner CSM/SE): review per-route latency and error rates, confirm no active Sev1/Sev2, verify usage vs committed capacity, validate function-calling success rates.
- Monthly (owner CSM): consolidated metrics and trends, cost optimization review (batching/quantization/cache), security/compliance scan status, document action items.

8) QBR agenda & template
- Suggested 60-90 min agenda: Executive summary; Operational health (uptime, p99); Cost & efficiency (per-token cost, Optimize recommendations); Roadmap & feature requests; Action items.
- QBR slide bullets: Adoption metrics, Performance (p50/p95/p99), Reliability (incidents, MTTR), Cost breakdown, Risks & open items.

9) Communication templates
- Sev1 notification subject: [Sev1] {CustomerName} - Production outage - initial notification. Body: brief outage summary, next update time, contacts: jordan.lee@redwood.ai and on-call pager.
- QBR invite subject: QBR — {CustomerName} & Redwood. Body: proposed agenda and requested attendees.

10) Metrics and SLOs (defaults)
- Availability SLO: 99.9% monthly for redwood-api (hosted). Latency SLO sample: p95 < 500ms for interactive on committed capacity. Error budget reviewed monthly; alert when burn > 50%.

11) Post-onboarding handoff
- Two-week stabilization: daily check-ins week 1, bi-weekly week 2. Handoff to account management and standard support. Document final config, routing, and one-off fixes in account playbook.

12) Appendix & links
- Integration benchmarking template: confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/benchmarking-and-perf-suite. Incident process: confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process. SLOs & error budget: confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets. Support ticketing: Zendesk KB internal link.

Change log: 2025-11-10 initial draft (Jordan Lee); 2026-02-15 added Sev defs and commands (Carlos Ruiz); 2026-03-04 revised known-issues and QBR template (Priya Desai).

Maintain this page for process changes and notify reviewers when updating.
